subject: Post-call: Sponsor alignment, decision rules, and compliance asks
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@novacorp.com>
Cc: Tom Baines <procurement@novacorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: key problems, goals, and proposed next steps

Elena — thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap and proposed path so we have alignment before you loop in legal and the board.

Summary of pain and goals (as we heard):
- Volume spike and latency sensitivity: search and recommendations pipeline needs 70% faster 99th percentile latency during peak traffic.
- Cost predictability: current spend on embeddings and generation is variable; finance needs a capped model to forecast Q1.
- Data residency & auditability: Nova needs per-request audit logs and retention controls for regulated lines of business.

Business outcomes you called out:
1) Improve end-user engagement by reducing model latency to support 50k concurrent sessions.
2) Reduce per-query inference cost by ~30% via batching + quantized model profiles.
3) Demonstrate audit trail and encryption-at-rest to satisfy compliance review by mid-Jan.

Risks we identified on the call:
- Procurement timeline: legal wants SOW + data processing addendum (DPA) before committing to a pilot.
- Platform constraints: on-prem networking performance could affect latency targets; we should validate in the pilot.

What we propose as next steps (simple decision path):
1) Redwood to deliver a short SOW + risk matrix draft (attached).
2) Schedule a 60-minute technical pilot scoping call this week with your infra and security leads.
3) We provision a dedicated pilot cluster (dedicated capacity) and run a 2-week performance validation against your traffic sample.
4) Procurement & legal review: we’ll provide a DPA template and a procurement checklist to accelerate contracting.

Immediate asks from NovaCorp: please confirm the executive sponsor (is it still you?) and share the procurement contact who owns contract sign-off. Tom (CC'd) — are you the right procurement contact?

Attachments: Novacorp_RiskMatrix_v1.xlsx (risk matrix / mitigation notes), Redwood_SOW_draft_20261130.pdf (SOW + pilot deliverables)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the scoping call once you confirm attendees.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132


From: Elena Ruiz <elena@novacorp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Baines <procurement@novacorp.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: key problems, goals, and proposed next steps

Marcus — thank you for the crisp recap. Confirmations:
- Sponsor: yes, I remain the executive sponsor for this initiative.
- Procurement: Tom is the right POC for contracting and will lead the procurement checklist. I’m looping Legal (legal@novacorp.com) once Tom flags the draft SOW.

A few clarifications from our side:
- The latency target you noted is aggressive — we need clear definition of traffic mix (interactive vs. batch) in the SOW.
- Regarding audit logs: we require per-request user identifiers (redacted for PII) plus a 7-year retention option for certain regulated flows. Can Redwood support this with private deployment?

I’m available for the scoping call Thursday morning PST. Tom — please confirm if that works and whether Legal needs the SOW before the scoping call.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
VP Product, NovaCorp
elena@novacorp.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: (internal)
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap — procurement & compliance posture (internal)

Marissa / Kimberly — forwarding the external thread. Key internal asks before scoping call:
1) Legal & DPA: Kimberly, can you confirm if our standard DPA covers 7-year optional retention clauses and per-request audit log exports, or do we need an addendum?
2) On-prem performance: Marissa, can Eng Ops prepare a short test plan to validate networking/latency on a representative private deployment (we should include sequence length distributions and peak concurrency numbers).
3) Pricing guardrails: we should propose a pilot pricing structure that includes a capped trial budget and a measurable SLA for 99th percentile latency.

Quick notes for the SOW: keep the pilot scope to 2 weeks, list success criteria (latency numbers, cost per 1k requests, audit export), and include an explicit rollback/fallback policy to hosted variant.

I attached an initial risk matrix; please annotate with legal/ops comments and return by EOD Wednesday so we can share with Nova ahead of the call.

—Marcus

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@novacorp.com>, Tom Baines <procurement@novacorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Executive sponsor summary & contracting path (next steps + deliverables)

Elena / Tom — following our thread and internal coordination, here is an executive-focused summary for your board and procurement packet. Please feel free to forward.

Outcome statement for sponsors:
- Objective: Validate Redwood Dedicated (private VPC) can meet NovaCorp's latency and audit requirements while reducing per-query cost by ~30% for the targeted workloads.
- Pilot scope: 2-week dedicated pilot using NovaCorp traffic sample (up to 50k concurrent sessions simulated, peak 99th latency target: <= 300ms).
- Success metrics: 99th pctl latency <= 300ms; per-query cost reduction >= 25% vs current baseline; delivery of per-request audit logs export and proof of retention mechanics.

Procurement path & timeline (recommended):
- Today (EOD): Redwood to send SOW + risk matrix (attached) and DPA template.
- Thu, 03 Dec: Technical scoping call (60 minutes) — infra, security, and engineering present.
- Week of 07 Dec: Pilot provisioning & initial validation.
- By 23 Dec: Pilot completion and readout.
- Contracting: If pilot passes, move to a 12-month Dedicated contract; procurement to aim for signature by mid-Jan.

Escalation items for board visibility:
- If legal requires significant DPA customization, this may push contracting past mid-Jan.
- If our private deployment tests show network bottlenecks, we will propose a staged rollout with hybrid hosting to meet business SLAs while remediation occurs.

Deliverables attached: Redwood_SOW_draft_20261130.pdf (SOW outline + pilot acceptance criteria), Novacorp_RiskMatrix_v1.xlsx (risk assessment and mitigations).

Next immediate asks:
1) Elena — confirm attendees for Thu scoping call (security, infra, procurement).
2) Tom — confirm procurement documentation process and whether Legal needs the SOW before the scoping call.
3) Marissa / Kimberly — please return annotated SOW/risk matrix by EOD Wed (2026-12-02).

Thanks — happy to jump on a separate leadership readout if it helps your board.

Best regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: Novacorp_RiskMatrix_v1.xlsx; Redwood_SOW_draft_20261130.pdf
